title: Chapter 43
content:
While Kang Il-hyun browsed through the ties in the display case, Jakyeong surveyed the expansive walk-in closet. Resembling a high-end luxury boutique, the wardrobe held an endless array of tailored shirts, slacks, designer leather shoes, belts, cufflinks, and luxury timepieces that looked as if an entire department store floor had been transplanted into the room. If Wang Han—who harbored an obsession with luxury fashion—had seen this, he would have lost his mind with envy.

As Jakyeong examined the watch display, Il-hyun called out to him.

"Come here a moment."

Il-hyun held several silk ties against Jakyeong's collar one by one, assessing the combinations.

"This one suits you better."

Unknotting the simple black tie Jakyeong was wearing, Il-hyun replaced it with one patterned in deep crimson. His hands moved with clean, fluid precision as he formed the Windsor knot. Looking down at those long, elegant fingers, Jakyeong wondered how many lives they had ended. At the very least, his body count rivals mine.

"What are you thinking about?"

Jakyeong lifted his gaze, meeting Il-hyun's dark eyes at point-blank range. Il-hyun offered an easy, charming smile, stepped back a pace to inspect his work, and nodded with satisfaction.

"Flawless."

"Thank you."

What did Chairman Kang intend to discuss tonight? The moment the patriarch called, Jakyeong had sensed this was far from a simple dinner invitation. The new silk tie felt constricting around his throat. Wang Han’s old assessment that Jakyeong was a terrible actor rang uncomfortably true; he had no idea what kind of expression he was supposed to keep before the old man.

"Go with an easy mind," Il-hyun said casually. "What could possibly happen?"

"..."

"Take the handgun with you, just in case."

Tells me nothing will happen, then tells me to pack heat. Finding the contradiction absurd, Jakyeong turned to leave without bothering to reply.

Il-hyun caught his forearm, pulling him back toward the display case before retrieving a velvet-lined box.

Lifting the lid, a luxury timepiece rested inside—a piece easily valued in the hundreds of thousands of dollars. Il-hyun wrapped the leather strap around Jakyeong's wrist, checking the fit with a slight tilt of his head.

"Why give me a watch...?"

"There's an explosive charge built into the casing," Il-hyun said smoothly. "Say anything foolish over there, and it detonates on the spot."

Having witnessed Choi Ki-tae's severed head delivered in a pastel gift box earlier that afternoon, the threat didn't sound entirely like a joke.

"Come to think of it, that wouldn't be a bad outcome," Il-hyun mused with a dark chuckle. "Saves me fifteen million dollars, and takes the old man out in the blast."

The moment Jakyeong reached to unbuckle the strap, Il-hyun caught his hand.

"I'm joking. It's a gift."

Jakyeong raised an eyebrow skeptically. "I'm already plenty satisfied with the gift you delivered earlier today."

The remark was drenched in dry sarcasm, but Il-hyun’s eyes crinkled with genuine amusement. Is he really that thrilled that I'm pleased Choi Ki-tae is dead?

When Il-hyun raised a hand toward his cheek, Jakyeong took a step back to avoid the touch, only to find his back pressed firmly against the full-length mirror behind him.

Il-hyun closed the distance, trapping him against the glass. The hand on his cheek smoothed down over his throat, shoulder, and chest. The moment calloused fingers brushed against his tender, inflamed chest, Jakyeong swatted the hand away with a sharp slap.

Il-hyun let out a low, vibrating chuckle. "Sensitive, aren't we?"

Jakyeong sneered back without missing a beat. "All thanks to you, Director Kang. After being gnawed on like a piece of raw meat, the skin is practically shredded."

"Ah, you were talking about your chest? I was referring to your mood."

"..."

"If you'd like, I can leave other parts of you thoroughly wrecked as well."

As Il-hyun's palm drifted down to cup his rear, Jakyeong pried the hand away, forcing a thin, strained smile. What he truly wanted was to put a bullet through Kang Il-hyun's skull and leave it in pieces. But Il-hyun was his employer—a fifteen-million-dollar ultra-VIP client.

Initially, Jakyeong had intended to flee the country the moment this contract concluded without looking back. But on second thought, if this lunatic offered another contract in the future with this caliber of payout, taking on one or two more jobs wasn't out of the question—provided it didn't involve sharing a bed.

Checking the watch on his wrist, Jakyeong cleared his throat. "It's time I left. If you'll excuse me—"

Before he could pull away, Il-hyun leaned down and captured his mouth.

Jakyeong considered shoving him off, but gave up, staring blankly up at the ceiling molding instead. Feeling the lack of resistance, Il-hyun’s hands began roaming over his waist and hips. Jakyeong tried to endure the touch along his flanks, but the moment large fingers firmly gripped his rear, he reached his limit, shoving hard against Il-hyun's broad shoulders.

Wiping the back of his hand across his mouth, Jakyeong glared. Il-hyun remained completely unfazed, wearing a smug, satisfied grin.

"Why is your face flushed? Enjoying yourself?"

Failing to distinguish pure, homicidal rage from arousal—the man is a certified psychopath.

"No. Frankly, that was the most underwhelming kiss of my entire life."

Jakyeong delivered the insult to wound the man's ego, and a flicker of sharp displeasure immediately crossed Il-hyun's dark pupils.

"Is that so?"

"I'm serious. It was enough to kill an erection on the spot."

"We can test that theory right now."

When Il-hyun stepped forward again, Jakyeong shoved him back and bolted out of the dressing room. Passing through the living room, he caught Park Tae-soo watching him from the sofa. Fuming with irritation, Jakyeong stomped up the stairs to his suite, making sure every footstep echoed loudly through the villa.

After asking the domestic staff for a glass of ice water, Jakyeong waited inside Chairman Kang’s private study.

Throughout the formal dinner, the patriarch had barely uttered a word. Wary of poison, Jakyeong had refrained from touching his plate, only picking up his chopsticks once the Chairman and Seok-joo had begun eating.

Sitting alone in the mahogany-lined study, the minutes ticked by with agonizing slowness.

Mounted on the wall was a framed family portrait—much older than the contemporary prints in the main foyer. Spotting a young Kang Il-hyun was effortless; looking significantly younger, the teenage boy wore an expression of sheer, murderous misery at being forced in front of the camera.

The double doors clicked open, and Chairman Kang entered, leaning on his polished wooden cane. A maid followed closely behind, setting a tray of hot tea on the low table before bowing out.

Settling into the leather armchair, the Chairman clipped a thick cigar and lit the tip.

"Did the meal suit your palate?"

"Yes, Chairman... It was delicious."

"I am glad to hear it. Care for a smoke?"

"No, thank you... I don't smoke cigars."

The old man let out a hearty, rumbling chuckle. "Wise choice. No sense picking up harmful habits. Quitting this wretched tobacco is a devilish task."

"Indeed... Haha."

"Humans are remarkably foolish creatures. We walk straight into hazards even while knowing the consequences."

Jakyeong held his tongue, keeping his posture deferential.

"How has your stay with Executive Director Kang been? No inconveniences, I trust?"

"As I mentioned before... the Director takes exceptional care of me."

"That is a relief. Ensuring your comfort is the only way I can save face before your esteemed grandfather."

Is he fishing for information? Suspicion naturally deepened with age in this line of work. Regardless of the subtext, maintaining the docile mask of Jang Yi-an was the only protocol.

The Chairman shared several anecdotes from the past—ranging from his early business dealings with Yi-an's father to his long-standing ties with Triad patriarch Jang Myeong.

As Jakyeong nodded and smiled along, a secretary entered the room—a clean-cut young man wearing spectacles and a mild, agreeable expression.

"What of the memorial wreaths?" the Chairman asked without looking up.

"Yes, sir. They are scheduled for dispatch this evening."

"Ensure the arrangements are immaculate. The deceased was a companion of Seok-joo; we must show proper respect."

"Understood, Chairman."

The secretary bowed and withdrew. Once the door clicked shut, Chairman Kang fixed a heavy, penetrating gaze onto Jakyeong.

"I assume you are aware of the matter? Choi Ki-tae. You spent time with him alongside Seok-joo, did you not?"

Jakyeong nodded quietly. "Yes, sir."

"He was found dead in his private office earlier today. Whoever the assailant was, they decapitated the boy and took the head with them."

Chairman Kang clicked his tongue in theatrical dismay, lamenting the depravity of the modern world.

Jakyeong sat in stunned silence. He had assumed Il-hyun’s cleanup crew would dispose of the remains discreetly; he never imagined the headless corpse had simply been abandoned on the office floor.

Putting on a look of delicate, frightened shock, Jakyeong asked for confirmation, prompting a weary sigh from the patriarch.

"So young... What a tragedy."

"Indeed, sir."

"It is a terrifying world we live in. There is no guarantee such a fate could not befall you, after all."

Jakyeong’s hand paused mid-air as he reached for his teacup.

He lifted his eyes to meet the Chairman's stare. The old man smiled pleasantly, grinding the burning tip of his cigar into the crystal ashtray with a slow hiss until the ember died.

Jakyeong’s mind raced behind his neutral mask. What was the calculation behind that veiled threat?

"Who could commit such a terrible act, Chairman?"

Chairman Kang stared through him with an unblinking, dissecting gaze. Jakyeong didn't flinch, deliberately softening the focus in his eyes to project the pure, naive innocence of a sheltered heir.

Slowly, the predator melted back into the guise of a kindly grandfather. Opening an ornate lacquer box on the desk, the Chairman offered Jakyeong a wrapped hard candy.

"How could an old man like me know? Though... I am reminded of a rather poignant maxim I once heard."

"..."

Leaning forward, the Chairman recited the words slowly, carving each syllable into the quiet room:

"There are those whom I trust will never bring me harm. I call them corpses."

Beneath the mahogany table, Jakyeong’s knuckles tightened against his knee.

The Chairman smiled warmly, asking if Jakyeong knew who had once spoken those very words to him. Jakyeong kept his silence.

Lifting his porcelain cup, Chairman Kang took a slow, leisurely sip of the hot tea.

"Word has reached my ears that you and Executive Director Kang have been spending quite a bit of intimate time together lately."

The remark was entirely unvarnished—a direct, probing strike. Who leaked that? Is there an informant among the domestic staff?

When Jakyeong maintained a tight, careful silence, the old man set his teacup down, his lips curving into a chilling, razor-thin smile.

"Do not place your absolute trust in anyone, young man. Regardless of who they may be."

The cold, predatory curvature of that smile was the spitting image of Kang Il-hyun’s—a visceral reminder that the same poisonous blood ran through both their veins.

Steam curled gently from the porcelain coffee mug in Kang Il-hyun's hand.

After an overcast afternoon, the sky had ruptured, unleashing a torrential downpour against the panoramic glass. Looking out into the deluge, the darkness in Il-hyun’s eyes mirrored the storm outside.

From an encrypted receiver sitting on the console, Chairman Kang’s voice crackled clearly through the private frequency:

[There are those whom I trust will never bring me harm. I call them corpses.]

"What a pathetic clown," Il-hyun scoffed aloud, openly mocking his father's words.

That was a line Il-hyun had spoken to the Chairman years ago. Over the wire, Lee Ja-kyeong remained remarkably sparse with his words—the exact tactical response called for in such a minefield.

[Do not place your absolute trust in anyone, young man. Regardless of who they may be.]

Il-hyun tapped the console, cutting the audio feed, and turned back to the leather sectional where Park Tae-soo was already seated.

Leaking the rumor to Chairman Kang that Il-hyun and Jang Yi-an were sharing a bed had been Il-hyun's own design. Predictably, the old man had summoned the boy under the guise of a family dinner, allowing suspicion to take root in his paranoid mind.

"Will this be acceptable, Director?" Tae-soo asked quietly. "The Chairman will begin actively probing your movements."

Il-hyun placed a fresh cigarette between his lips, his face lighting up with genuine, predatory amusement.

"That is precisely the objective. How else do you expect the old tiger to make a move?"

Chairman Kang had contracted a covert hit through black-market brokers and systematically scrubbed every digital paper trail. Merely catching a non-lethal sniper round at the inauguration was insufficient leverage; Il-hyun required ironclad, undeniable proof that the patriarch had orchestrated the assassination attempt.

To force that evidence into the light, he needed to exploit the old man's deep-seated paranoia. When a cornered predator feels the walls closing in, desperation sets in—and desperate men always make fatal mistakes.
